chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari and Muhammad ibn Yahya together, from Ahmad ibn Is'haq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
'And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them'
He said: 'We, by God, are the most beautiful names (al-Asma' al-Husna), without whose recognition God does not accept any deed from His servants.'

key_terms.الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى: The most beautiful names — theologically, God's names and attributes; here interpreted as the Imams of the Ahlulbayt
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a divine epithet used when mentioning God
key_terms.مَعْرِفَة: Recognition, gnosis, acknowledgment — knowing and accepting the Imams' authority

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of al-Asma al-Husna (most beautiful names) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides an esoteric Shia interpretation of Quran 7:180, where 'the most beautiful names of God' are identified with the Imams of the Ahlulbayt. The Imam declares that God will not accept any deed from His servants without the recognition (ma'rifa) of the Imams — meaning that acknowledgment of their authority and spiritual guidance is a precondition for the acceptance of all worship and good deeds. This hadith reflects the central Shia doctrine of wilaya (guardianship/authority of the Imams) and its absolute necessity for a believer's deeds to be spiritually valid.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary and Muhammad Bin Yahya, altogether from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [7:180]
And Allah's are the Best Names, therefore call on Him by these.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup>, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, are ‘الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى’ the good names which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will not be Accepting the deeds from the servants except (if they are) with our<sup>asws</sup> recognition’.
en.sarwar: 4. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ari and Muhammad ibn Yahya altogether have narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Su‘dan ibn Muslim from Mu‘awiya ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following about the words of Allah. “
God has the most blessed Names. You should address Him in your worship by these Names . .” [7:180]
The Imam said, “We, I swear by Allah, are the most blessed names of Allah without which Allah does not accept any of the good deeds of His servants until they know us properly.”
